title: Adaptive microqueue watermarking with tenant-aware KV tiered spillover
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem: Under sustained, high QPS traffic we observe repeated microburst events where microbatch queues fill and force large KV cache evictions or GPU OOMs. Existing admission logic is fast but blind to tenant traffic shape and to KV hotness tiers, which causes noisy neighbor effects and long tail P99 latencies for critical tenants.

Goal: Implement an adaptive microqueue watermarking algorithm that operates per-tenant and signals tier-aware KV spillover decisions. The design should: (1) avoid global hard caps that penalize low-latency tenants, (2) prioritize KV retention for hot keys by tenant/service criticality, and (3) implement progressive backpressure signals (watermarks) and a controlled spillover path that moves cold KV entries to host-managed spill (CPU/NVMe) before evicting GPU-resident hot entries.

Success criteria: reduced P99 token latency for high-priority tenants by >=20% under synthetic 2x baseline QPS bursts, GPU memory OOMs eliminated in replay tests, and overall throughput impact <=5% in steady-state load.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness reproduces burst pattern used in incident-2026-01 and demonstrates P99 reduction >=20% for priority tenants
No GPU OOMs in 24h stress test at 2x production QPS with mixed-tenancy workload
Metrics: new per-tenant microqueue_fill_ratio and kv_tier_spill_rate are exposed; alert thresholds documentated
Rollback-safe: feature gated and controlled by runtime flags + canary rollout to 5% of serving fleet
Code reviewed and load-tested; PR merged and automated test coverage for watermark transitions added
design_notes: Introduce microqueue watermarks: low/medium/high per-tenant thresholds derived from EWMA of arrival rate and recent tail latency
Watermark actions: low=hint batcher to favor latency, medium=allow controlled microbatching increase, high=emit soft backpressure token that triggers KV tier spill decisions
KV tiering: hot (GPU-resident), warm (host-RAM caching), cold (NVMe spill). Spill policy favors moving cold keys first; tenant priority is a multiplier on hotness score
Spill mechanism: asynchronous background spill thread with bounded concurrency to avoid CPU saturation; maintain graceful read-path fallback to warm/cold tiers
Admission controller changes: decouple microqueue admission decisions from global GPU headroom; add tenant weight and predicted tail-risk factor
Metrics instrumentation: per-tenant queue length histogram, watermark state timeline, kv_tier_sizes, spill_latency_histogram, and GPU free-slot gauge
Trade-offs: introducing spill paths increases read latency for cold keys; mitigated by prefetch heuristics for frequently accessed cold keys and tenant-priority boosting
Alternatives considered: stronger global throttling (rejected for tenant fairness), evict-on-write policy (rejected due to poor tail behavior)
implementation_tasks: Bench: extend perf harness to replay incident-2026-01 burst traces (ENG-121456-BENCH)
Runtime: add per-tenant watermark controller and integrate with microbatch allocator (ENG-121456-RUNTIME)
KV: implement tiered spill queue with eviction prioritizer and bounded async spill workers (ENG-121456-KV)
Middleware: expose runtime flags and tenant-priority config in control plane + console feature toggle (ENG-121456-CONFIG)
Tests: unit tests for watermark transitions, integration tests for spill path correctness, end-to-end load tests (ENG-121456-TEST)
Docs: design doc in Confluence and runbook for incident response (ENG-121456-DOC)
Canary: rollout plan and automated rollback hook (ENG-121456-CANARY)
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Lab validation using synthetic bursts (feature flag on) — target 2 engineers for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Canary to 5% of serving fleet with high-priority tenant routing — monitor P50/P95/P99 and kv spill rates for 72h
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% with expanded telemetry and operator-run checks
Phase 4: Full rollout after 7 days with no regressions; enable automatic spill backoff thresholds
Rollback: disable feature flag and trigger immediate spill abort; tracked in runbook
monitoring_and_alerts: New metrics: tenant_microqueue_fill_ratio (gauge), tenant_watermark_state (enum), kv_tier_spill_rate (counters by tier)
Alerts: tenant_microqueue_fill_ratio>0.9 for 30s AND kv_tier_spill_rate_spike => pager (P0)
SLO checks: daily regression job verifies P99 under standard workload not worse than baseline
Dashboards: add a microqueue-overview panel and tenant-level drilldown in console/runtime dashboards
risks_and_mitigation: Increased cold-read latency: mitigate with adaptive prefetch and tenant-priority caching
Spill worker overload: bound concurrency and backpressure on spill queue; autoscaling spill workers not allowed unless safe
Complexity and bugs in watermark transitions: add exhaustive state-machine unit tests and chaos tests
Incorrect hotness scoring could starve tenants: expose hotness debug endpoints and provide manual override per-tenant
